title: Dimension is the degree of a projective Hilbert polynomial
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $N\geq0$, and let $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_K$ be a nonempty closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-projective]. Let $P_X\in\mathbf Q[t]$ be its Hilbert polynomial: for all sufficiently large integers $m$, $P_X(m)$ is the dimension of the degree-$m$ part of the homogeneous coordinate ring. Then $P_X(m)=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$ for every integer $m$, $P_X$ is nonzero, its leading coefficient is positive, and $\deg P_X=\dim X$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. In particular, if $P_X(m)=dm+e$ with $d>0$, then $X$ has dimension one. The polynomial and this dimension conclusion are unchanged by extension of $K$. No reducedness, equidimensionality or irreducibility is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BEM (lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler) and 0BEV (lemma-ample-positive): the coefficient of degree dim X is the positive top self-intersection divided by (dim X)!. Equality with the eventual coordinate-ring polynomial also uses the Hilbert polynomial discussion of coherent.tex; see lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality.

proof.text: The specified embedding makes $X$ projective by [def-kun-projective], hence proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] makes $g=\dim X$ finite; since $X$ is nonempty, $g$ is a nonnegative integer. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are zero and itself, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. In particular its structure sheaf is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]: locally it is the free rank-one module.

source.place: Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); coherent.tex Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian); finite dimension as in lem-kun-dimension-finite-type

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_K}(1)$. It is ample by [lem-pc-very-ample-ample]. The bases and transition rules of [def-pc-projective-space-twist], pulled back using [def-pc-module-pullback], give $\mathcal O_X(m)$ transition functions $i^*(x_a/x_b)^m$. Multiplying these functions identifies $\mathcal O_X(m)$ with $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$; for negative $m$ use the dual bases. These local free rank-one descriptions also make all twists quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth].

source.place: Twisting sheaves on projective space; properties.tex Tag 01Q3 (ample criterion); coherent.tex Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial] with $r=1$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal L_1=\mathcal L$. Its support is all of $X$: at every scheme point the structure-sheaf stalk is a nonzero local ring. Thus it supplies $Q\in\mathbf Q[t]$ of degree at most $g$ with $Q(m)=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$ for every integer $m$. In [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial], the degree-$m$ vanishing polynomials form a vector subspace: restriction of a linear combination is the same linear combination of the restrictions. Thus taking their linear span does not change this subspace. Its $I_m(i)$ is exactly the degree-$m$ ideal piece of [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal], so its coordinate piece is $(K[x_0,\ldots,x_N]/J)_m$. By that identification, write the given closed subscheme as $\operatorname{Proj}(K[x_0,\ldots,x_N]/J)$. The eventual coordinate/Euler equality of [lem-sfb-projective-coordinate-ring-euler-polynomial] shows that $Q(m)$ and the prescribed $P_X(m)$ agree for all sufficiently large natural $m$. Their difference has infinitely many rational roots, hence is zero. Consequently $P_X=Q$, proving equality with Euler characteristics at every integer and the bound $\deg P_X\leq g$.

source.place: Tag 0BEM (lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler); constructions.tex Tag 03GL (lemma-closed-in-projective-space); coherent.tex Tag 0AG7 (lemma-recover-tail-graded-module), with varieties.tex Tag 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0)

proof.text: Use the current Hilbert-degree definition of [sk-def-av-ample-degree]: if $a_g$ is the coefficient of $t^g$ in $P_X$, then $D=\deg_{\mathcal L}(X)=g!a_g$. This is the finite-difference definition, also recorded in the main-20261015 update of [def-sc-hilbert-degree]. The hypotheses of [lem-sc-positive-ample-hilbert-degree] hold by steps 1 and 2: $X$ is nonempty and proper, and $\mathcal L$ is ample invertible. Hence $D>0$. Since $g!>0$, we have $a_g>0$. Therefore $P_X\ne0$ and $\deg P_X\geq g$; step 3 gives the opposite inequality. Thus $\deg P_X=g$, and its leading coefficient is $a_g>0$. This includes $g=0$, since $0!=1$.

source.place: Tag 0BEV (lemma-ample-positive), with Tag 0BEP (definition-intersection-number); the coefficient interpretation is the current blueprint sk-def-av-ample-degree

proof.text: If $P_X(t)=dt+e$ with $d>0$, its coefficient of $t$ is nonzero and every coefficient above $t$ is zero. Thus its degree is exactly one. The equality proved in step 4 gives $\dim X=1$.

source.place: Immediate polynomial consequence of Tag 0BEV and the preceding steps

proof.text:
Let $L/K$ be any field extension. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $X_L$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^N_L$, and [lem-pc-proper-base-change] makes it proper. The pulled-back transition functions in step 2 are $(x_a/x_b)^m$ over $L$, so the pullback of $\mathcal O_X(m)$ is exactly $\mathcal O_{X_L}(m)$ for every integer $m$; this follows directly from [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and [def-pc-module-pullback]. The map $K\to L$ is flat: short exact sequences of $K$-vector spaces split by choosing bases, and tensoring their direct-sum decompositions with $L$ preserves exactness. Apply the general clause of [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] to $\mathcal O_X(m)$. For every $q\geq0$ it gives
$$H^q(X_L,\mathcal O_{X_L}(m))\cong H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(m))\otimes_KL.$$
These groups on $X$ are finite dimensional and vanish outside a finite set of $q$ by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined]. The tensor flip $v\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes v$, with the same formula as inverse, identifies these with $L\otimes_K H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(m))$. Thus [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change] applies in its stated tensor order and preserves their dimensions. Taking the finite alternating sums of [def-pc-euler-characteristic] gives $\chi(X_L,\mathcal O_{X_L}(m))=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(m))=P_X(m)$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$.

Apply [lem-sfb-projective-coordinate-ring-euler-polynomial] to the closed subscheme $X_L\subset\mathbf P^N_L$, presenting it by the homogeneous ideal supplied by [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal]. Together with step 6 this says that $P_X$ is also its eventual coordinate polynomial; uniqueness follows again from infinitely many values. The last clause of [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality] says that a projective scheme over any field has zero Hilbert polynomial exactly when it is empty. Since $P_X\ne0$, $X_L$ is nonempty. The argument of steps 1--4, already established for an arbitrary field and closed embedding, therefore applies over $L$ and gives $\dim X_L=\deg P_X=\dim X$. The linear-polynomial conclusion of step 5 holds over $L$ as well. None of these steps used reducedness, irreducibility, or equidimensionality.
